knowledge_bases.title: HR Policies
knowledge_bases.description:
Contains: this company's HR Leave Policy document (PDF), plus short FAQ entries covering password reset and login issues, checking vacation/PTO balance, where to find the org chart, employee benefits, the holiday schedule, how to contact HR, first-day onboarding steps, and payroll timing.

When to search this:
- Leave and time-off policy questions, which the HR Leave Policy document covers in detail
- The specific FAQ topics listed above

When NOT to search this:
- Code of conduct, POSH/harassment, expenses and reimbursement, remote-work rules, notice period, termination or probation — no material on these is loaded
- Any individual employee's own leave balance, attendance, payroll or appraisal records
- Anything needing a specific employee's data rather than general policy text

Note: several FAQ entries are generic sample text and may not reflect this company's actual practice; the HR Leave Policy document is the authoritative source.

sources.title: FAQ : Benefits
sources.content:
Topic: Employee Benefits
Category: Benefits

Q: What benefits does the company offer?
A: The company offers a comprehensive benefits package including:
- Medical, dental, and vision insurance (multiple plan options)
- 401(k) retirement plan with company matching up to 4%
- Life insurance and AD&D coverage
- Short-term and long-term disability insurance
- Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
- Flexible Spending Account (FSA) and Health Savings Account (HSA)
- Commuter benefits
- Tuition reimbursement (up to $5,250 per year)
- Gym membership discount

Q: When can I enroll in benefits?
A: Benefits enrollment is available during:
- New hire enrollment window: within 30 days of your start date
- Annual open enrollment: held each November for the following calendar year
- Qualifying life events (marriage, divorce, birth/adoption of child, loss of other coverage) within 30 days of the event

Q: How do I change my benefits elections?
A: Outside of open enrollment, you can only change benefits due to a qualifying life event. Submit your change request in the HR Portal under "Benefits" > "Change Request" within 30 days of the qualifying event.

Q: What is the 401(k) match policy?
A: The company matches 50% of your contributions up to 8% of your salary, meaning a maximum match of 4%. You are fully vested in company contributions after 3 years of service.

Q: How do I contact the benefits administrator?
A: Contact the Benefits Team at benefits@company.com or call (555) 123-4569. For insurance carrier questions, refer to your benefits guide for carrier contact information.

sources.title: FAQ : HR Contact
sources.content:
Topic: HR Contact Information and Support
Category: HR Support

Q: How do I contact the HR team?
A: HR Team Contact Information:
- Email: hr@company.com
- Phone: (555) 123-4567
- Office Location: Building A, 2nd Floor, Room 210
- Hours: Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM (Eastern Time)

Q: What issues does HR handle?
A: The HR team handles a wide range of topics, including:
- Employee onboarding and offboarding
- Benefits enrollment and questions
- Leave of absence and FMLA requests
- Workplace complaints and investigations
- Performance management and reviews
- Compensation and salary questions
- Company policy clarifications
- Training and development programs

Q: Is there an HR emergency contact?
A: For urgent or after-hours HR matters, email hr-urgent@company.com. For workplace safety emergencies, call building security at (555) 123-9999 or dial 911 for life-threatening emergencies.

Q: How do I submit a confidential HR concern?
A: You can submit a confidential concern through the Ethics Hotline at https://ethics.company.com or call (800) 555-0100. Reports can be submitted anonymously.

Q: How long does it take for HR to respond?
A: Standard HR inquiries are answered within 2 business days. Escalated tickets are prioritized by urgency: urgent issues within 4 hours, high priority within 1 business day, and medium/low priority within 2-3 business days.

sources.title: FAQ : Onboarding
sources.content:
Topic: Onboarding and New Employee Information
Category: Onboarding

Q: What should I do on my first day?
A: On your first day:
1. Report to the reception desk in Building A – security will have your visitor badge ready
2. You will meet your HR onboarding contact for a welcome session
3. Your manager will provide a team introduction and first-week schedule
4. IT will set up your laptop and accounts (allow up to 2 hours)
5. You will complete required compliance training modules online

Q: How long does onboarding take?
A: The formal onboarding process spans your first 90 days (30-60-90 day plan). You will have check-ins with HR and your manager to review your progress and address any questions.

Q: What documents do I need to bring on my first day?
A: Bring two forms of identification for I-9 verification (e.g., passport, driver's license + Social Security card). A full list of acceptable documents is in your offer letter package.

Q: When will I receive my employee ID and badge?
A: Your employee ID is assigned before your start date and sent via email. Your physical access badge will be ready for pickup at Security on your first day.

Q: Who is my onboarding contact in HR?
A: You will be assigned a dedicated HR onboarding specialist before your start date. Their contact information will be in your pre-boarding email. You can also reach general HR onboarding support at onboarding@company.com.

Q: When does my benefits enrollment start?
A: Your benefits are effective on your first day of employment. You must complete your enrollment elections within 30 days of your start date through the HR Portal.

sources.title: FAQ : Org Chart
sources.content:
Topic: Organization Chart and Company Structure
Category: Company Information

Q: Where can I find the organization chart?
A: The organization chart is available on the company intranet at https://intranet.company.com under "About Us" > "Our Team". It is updated monthly by the HR team.

Q: How do I find out who my skip-level manager is?
A: The org chart on the intranet shows the full reporting hierarchy. You can also ask your direct manager or contact HR at hr@company.com for clarification.

Q: How are departments structured?
A: The company is organized into the following main departments: Engineering, Product, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, and Operations. Each department is led by a Vice President who reports to the C-suite.

Q: How do I find a colleague's contact information?
A: Employee contact information, including email addresses and phone extensions, is available in the company directory on the intranet under "Directory". You can search by name, department, or location.

Q: Who do I contact if the org chart is out of date?
A: Please email hr@company.com if you notice any inaccuracies in the organization chart. Org chart updates are processed within 5 business days of a confirmed organizational change.

sources.title: FAQ : Password Reset
sources.content:
Topic: Password Reset and Login Issues
Category: IT Support / Account Access

Q: How do I reset my password?
A: To reset your password, visit the IT Self-Service Portal at https://itportal.company.com. Click "Forgot Password" and follow the on-screen instructions. A reset link will be sent to your registered email address.

Q: Who do I contact for login problems?
A: Contact the IT Help Desk at helpdesk@company.com or call (555) 987-6543. The IT Help Desk is available Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 6 PM.

Q: What are the password requirements?
A: Passwords must be at least 12 characters long and include uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and at least one special character. Passwords expire every 90 days.

Q: I am locked out of my account. What should I do?
A: After 5 failed login attempts your account will be locked. You can unlock it via the IT Self-Service Portal or contact the IT Help Desk at helpdesk@company.com.

Q: Can I use my work login for personal devices?
A: Company credentials should only be used on approved corporate devices or through the company VPN. Do not store your credentials in personal browsers.

sources.title: FAQ : Payroll
sources.content:
Topic: Payroll and Salary
Category: Finance / Compensation

Q: When is payday?
A: Payroll is processed bi-weekly on Fridays. Direct deposits arrive in your bank account by 9 AM on payday. Paper checks, if requested, are distributed by end of business on the same Friday.

Q: How do I view my pay stub?
A: Pay stubs are available in the HR Portal under "Payroll" > "Pay Stubs". You can view and download your last 24 months of pay stubs at any time.

Q: What do I do if I notice an error in my pay?
A: Immediately contact Payroll at payroll@company.com or call (555) 123-4568. Provide your employee ID, pay period in question, and a description of the discrepancy. Corrections are typically processed in the next pay cycle.

Q: How do I update my direct deposit information?
A: Log into the HR Portal, navigate to "Payroll" > "Direct Deposit", and update your bank account details. Changes must be submitted at least 5 business days before the next pay date to take effect.

Q: Are overtime payments included in the bi-weekly paycheck?
A: Yes, approved overtime hours worked within the pay period are included in the same bi-weekly paycheck. Overtime must be pre-approved by your manager.

Q: Who do I contact about my W-2 or tax forms?
A: W-2 forms are mailed and available digitally in the HR Portal by January 31st each year. For questions, contact payroll@company.com.

sources.title: FAQ : Vacation
sources.content:
Topic: Vacation and PTO Balance
Category: Time Off / Leave

Q: How do I check my vacation balance?
A: Log into the HR Portal and navigate to "Time Off" > "Balances". You will see your current vacation, sick leave, and personal day balances. If you see any discrepancies, contact hr@company.com.

Q: How much vacation time do I accrue?
A: Vacation accrual is based on years of service:
- 0-2 years: 10 days (80 hours) per year
- 3-5 years: 15 days (120 hours) per year
- 6-10 years: 20 days (160 hours) per year
- 10+ years: 25 days (200 hours) per year

Vacation is accrued at an equal rate per pay period throughout the year.

Q: Can I carry over unused vacation days?
A: Employees may carry over up to 5 vacation days (40 hours) into the next calendar year. Any unused days beyond this limit will be forfeited on December 31st.

Q: How do I request time off?
A: Submit time off requests through the HR Portal under "Time Off" > "Request Time Off". Requests should be submitted at least 2 weeks in advance for planned vacations. Your manager will approve or deny the request within 3 business days.

Q: Can I cash out unused vacation?
A: Vacation cash-out is permitted once per year during the annual election period in November, up to 5 days (40 hours). Contact payroll@company.com for details.

Q: What is PTO and how is it different from vacation?
A: PTO (Paid Time Off) is a combined bank of vacation, sick leave, and personal days for eligible employees. Some legacy roles track these separately. Check your HR Portal to see which plan applies to you.
